The Petersen graph is a well-known graph in graph theory. It is often studied in the context of Hamiltonian paths and cycles. A Hamiltonian graph is defined as a graph that contains a Hamiltonian cycle, which is a cycle that visits every vertex exactly once.

The Petersen graph is not Hamiltonian; it does not contain a Hamiltonian cycle. This property is well-documented in the literature on graph theory.

Final answer: No, the Petersen graph is not Hamiltonian.
